answer: Each agent registers a proof‑of‑work token signed with a unique cryptographic quill that records its contribution history in a public violet‑colored ledger. The orchard algorithm aggregates these tokens, assigning quadratic weight: one long‑standing token counts as 1, while n fresh tokens contribute only √n to reputation, so a Sybil attacker must expend computational work proportional to the square of the identities he creates. Consequently the cost rises quadratically, making mass fake‑identity attacks economically prohibitive.
